section_summary.extract_value: The section reports that ethnic identity (MEIM) is positively associated with body appreciation (BAS), self-esteem (RSES), and appearance evaluation, and negatively associated with several eating- and weight-related concerns. The authors tested whether Western beauty ideal internalization (SATAQ-3 Internalization-General) mediated relations between ethnic identity and outcomes using 5,000 bootstrap resamples; mediation was found for eating concern, shape concern, and weight concern but not for body appreciation.
section_summary.evidence_source: "As hypothesized, ethnic identity, as measured by the MEIM, was positively associated with body appreciation (BAS);" and "Based on 95% confidence intervals for the indirect effects, Western beauty ideal internalization mediated the relation between ethnic identity and eating concern (−.35, −.01), ethnic identity and shape concern (−.56, −.01), and ethnic identity and weight concern (−.60, −.02). No mediating relation was found for ethnic identity and body appreciation (−.01, .24)."

Mediation analyses using bootstrapped resamples tested Western beauty ideal internalization (SATAQ-3 Internalization-General) as a mediator; it mediated relations between ethnic identity and eating/shape/weight concerns but not between ethnic identity and body appreciation. No explicit mention of 'Study 1' or multiple studies appears in this section.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports that ethnic identity (MEIM) was positively associated with body appreciation (BAS), moderately positively related to self-esteem (RSES), and had small positive associations with appearance evaluation (MBSRQ-AE). MEIM scores had small but significant negative associations with Western beauty ideal internalization and with eating, shape, and weight concerns, and were not significantly associated with specific eating-disordered behaviors. Bootstrapped mediation analyses (5,000 resamples) tested Western beauty ideal internalization (SATAQ-3 Internalization-General) as a mediator; it significantly mediated relations between ethnic identity and eating concern, shape concern, and weight concern (95% CIs reported), but did not mediate the relation between ethnic identity and body appreciation.
section_summary.evidence_source: "As hypothesized, ethnic identity, as measured by the MEIM, was positively associated with body appreciation (BAS) ... Ethnic identity also had a moderate, positive relation with self-esteem (RSES) and a small, positive association with appearance evaluation (MBSRQ AE)." "Based on 95% confidence intervals for the indirect effects, Western beauty ideal internalization mediated the relation between ethnic identity and eating concern (−.35, −.01), ethnic identity and shape concern (−.56, −.01), and ethnic identity and weight concern (−.60, −.02). No mediating relation was found for ethnic identity and body appreciation (−.01, .24)."
